questions.question: Eight producers each publish 180 messages/second and retries add 5% more deliveries. What ingress rate should capacity planning use?
questions.explanation: Base ingress is 8 x 180 = 1,440 messages/second. Retry inflation makes it 1,440 x 1.05 = 1,512 attempted deliveries per second.

questions.question: A queue has 10 partitions, 6 consumer instances, and each instance handles one message at a time. What limits parallel consumption first?
questions.explanation: Parallel workers are bounded by the smaller of assigned consumers and partitions. Six consumers can run only six concurrent partition assignments.

questions.question: Why can an at-least-once consumer apply a side effect twice even when it acknowledges only after work succeeds?
options: The acknowledgement can be lost after the effect commits
questions.explanation: If the business effect commits but the broker never observes the acknowledgement, the broker may redeliver the message. The consumer needs idempotency or another duplicate-safe effect.

questions.question: Which sequence is required for an effectively-once business outcome from an at-least-once queue?
options: Acknowledge first, then write the effect
Store a stable message identity with the effect, then acknowledge
Increase partition count, then retry forever
questions.explanation: The consumer records the business effect and processed-message identity atomically where possible. A later delivery sees the same identity and becomes a no-op before acknowledgement.

questions.question: What trade-off does retrying a poison message in place make?
options: It preserves order for that partition but blocks later work there
It guarantees global ordering across all partitions
It removes the need for an operator
questions.explanation: Holding the partition keeps later messages from passing the failing one, which preserves that partition's sequence but consumes availability until the failure is fixed.

questions.question: A producer is faster than the consumers for ten minutes. What is the most direct early-warning signal of user-visible delay?
questions.explanation: Queue depth shows accumulated work, but backlog age or consumer lag shows how long the oldest work has waited. It is the clearer indicator of delayed outcomes.
